read: full: main text pp. 1-12 (abstract, introduction, related work, section 3 on BBH's limits, section 4 construction, section 5 results and analyses, conclusion); appendix task descriptions pp. 17-36 skimmed, with the Disambiguation QA construction and verification read (p. 21).
venue_now: The file is arXiv:2502.19187v2 (6 May 2025; page 1 footer, Google DeepMind header dated 2025-5-7) and shows no venue. The May entry and papers.json give ACL 2025 (Long Papers), pp. 26473-26501.
what_it_is: BIG-Bench Extra Hard replaces each of BBH's 23 tasks with a new, harder task that probes a similar reasoning skill, because BBH had saturated, with state-of-the-art models above 90% (pp. 1-3). Tasks are adapted from existing datasets or written by the authors, and were made harder semi-adversarially until two Gemini reference models scored below 70% (p. 5); each task has 200 questions, Disambiguation QA 120 (p. 5). Answers are scored automatically and deterministically, and the headline is harmonic-mean accuracy across tasks: 9.8% for the best general-purpose model and 44.8% for the best reasoning model at release (pp. 1, 8-9).
domain: general reasoning (temporal, spatial, causal, deductive, linguistic, humour, sarcasm, arithmetic, algorithmic); not mathematics- or science-specific
size: 23 tasks of 200 questions each except Disambiguation QA with 120 (p. 5), i.e. 4,520 questions (derived, not stated); BBEH Mini of 460 (p. 7); 12 models plus a random baseline (Table 2, p. 9)
source_of_items: adapted from existing datasets (e.g. BoardgameQA, Dyck-language error finding, Linguini, New Yorker captions, SpatialLLMEval, SportQA, Test of Time, LiveBench web of lies, zebra puzzles) or written or generated by the authors (Table 1, p. 6; appendix)
instances: static (one fixed released set; some tasks were generated programmatically during construction, e.g. Boolean expressions and zebra puzzles, per the appendix)
has_gold_traces: no. Two tasks ask the model to find the first mistake in a given reasoning trace (Dyck Languages, and a Word Sorting subtask; Table 1, p. 6), but no gold reasoning is provided for scoring the model's own steps.
evaluation: final answer with automatic, deterministic scoring (p. 2); harmonic-mean accuracy across tasks as the headline, micro average for BBEH Mini (p. 8)
human_validation: none for the benchmark as a whole; the 120 author-written Disambiguation QA items each had an independent second check with adjudication, which led to 25 modifications (p. 21)
contamination_measures: none stated; the benchmark is released publicly on GitHub (p. 1)

engtrace_use.sentence: First, static benchmarks like Glue (Wang et al., 2019) and BBH (Kazemi et al., 2025) are increasingly prone to model saturation (Ott et al., 2022) and data contamination (Deng et al., 2024); EngTrace counters this through symbolic templates and domain-aware parameterization, generating unique, physically grounded problems that resist rote memorization. (S-I3, May L97-105)
engtrace_use.explanation: The sentence names BBH and cites this paper, which introduces BIG-Bench Extra Hard, the successor built because BBH had saturated (C2). As an example of a saturating benchmark it is the opposite case: at publication its best model reached 44.8% harmonic-mean accuracy (p. 1; Table 2, p. 9). The paper does document BBH's saturation, with state-of-the-art models above 90% accuracy (p. 1) and BBH dropping out of model evaluation reports (p. 3), so it is the right source for that fact if cited under its own name, next to Suzgun et al. for BBH itself. It says nothing about data contamination.

suggested_wording: BIG-Bench Hard (Suzgun et al., 2023) became saturated, with state-of-the-art models above 90% accuracy, and was succeeded by the harder BIG-Bench Extra Hard (Kazemi et al., 2025).
facts_to_cite: BBH became saturated, with state-of-the-art models achieving over 90% accuracy (p. 1), which caused it to disappear from recent model evaluation reports (p. 3).
BBEH replaces each of BBH's 23 tasks with a harder task testing a similar reasoning skill (pp. 2, 5; Table 1, p. 6).
Tasks were hardened semi-adversarially until two Gemini reference models scored below 70% (p. 5).
At release the best harmonic-mean accuracy was 9.8% for a general-purpose model and 44.8% for a reasoning-specialised model, against a random baseline of 8.4% (pp. 1, 8-9; Table 2, p. 9).

BBH's limitations named by the authors: a high random-chance baseline (8 of 23 tasks binary, 5 more with at most five options), shortcuts, short inputs (macro average 700 characters) and few reasoning hops (p. 3).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares automatic final-answer scoring and the concern with saturation. Lacks generated instances (a fixed released set), gold traces, step-level evaluation of the model's own reasoning (error-finding in given traces is a task, not a scoring method), any engineering domain, and validation of an evaluator against experts. Its answer to saturation is harder items; EngTrace's template generation answers contamination, not difficulty, and EngTrace's own answer scores are already 0.805 to 0.970 (engtrace_state_brief.md section 4).
notes: Name clash (C2): 'BBH' is cited to BBEH; add suzgun2022bbh if BBH stays named.
